signature.name: Notre-Dame de la Garde
signature.detail: Marseille's most famous sight, a hilltop basilica crowned by a golden statue of the Virgin that watches over the whole city and the sea. The climb rewards you with sweeping views over the harbor and the Calanques. Go early in the morning or near sunset for the best light and fewer crowds; you can walk up or take the bus.

signature.name: Calanques National Park
signature.detail: A dramatic stretch of limestone coves and turquoise water right at the city's edge, the reason many people fall in love with Marseille. Hiking the coastal trails or taking a boat trip is the classic way to see it. In summer some calanques close on hot, fire-risk days, so check access before you go and bring water.

signature.name: MuCEM
signature.detail: A striking modern museum on the waterfront, linked to the old Fort Saint-Jean by footbridges, devoted to Mediterranean cultures. Even if you skip the exhibitions, the building and rooftop views are worth the trip. The outdoor areas and fort are free to wander; go late afternoon for cooler air and harbor light.

signature.name: Cathédrale de la Major
signature.detail: A vast, striped Romanesque-Byzantine cathedral near the port, far bigger and more ornate than most visitors expect. It sits beside the MuCEM and the Joliette district, so it fits easily into a waterfront walk. Entry is free; dress respectfully and avoid visiting during services.

signature.name: Palais Longchamp
signature.detail: A grand 19th-century palace built around a monumental water fountain, with gardens and museums on either side. It is a favorite spot for a relaxed stroll away from the port crowds. Come in the morning for quiet gardens, and check museum opening days before planning a visit.

signature.name: Orange Velodrome
signature.detail: Marseille's iconic football stadium, home of Olympique de Marseille and famous for its roaring atmosphere on match days. Even outside games, it is a landmark of the city's sporting identity. Tickets for matches sell fast, so book well ahead and arrive early for the walk from the metro.

transport: Metro or tram about $2 a ride; day pass around $6
